tasks.description: grok-cli and Helix speak different OKF protocols today; define ONE canonical v1 contract and contract-test both clients against it.
tasks.details: 2026-10-04 FINDING (John's Drive upload): the 'OKF server software' is byte-identical to Helix's own src/okf/ module — there is no standalone server. KEY INSIGHT: Helix was designed to BE its own OKF server: src/io/web_server/mod.rs already mounts /okf/status, /okf/registry, /okf/health, /okf/schema, POST /okf/webhook (public) and POST /okf/reload, /okf/reload/force, /okf/manifest (protected), gated on [helix.okf] enabled (default false). BUT Helix's own fetcher (src/okf/fetcher.rs) requests endpoints the server does NOT mount: GET /okf/manifest.json, GET /okf/bundles/{id}/manifest.json, GET /okf/knowledge/{kid}. So Helix cannot serve itself — the server half and client half disagree on paths. The v1 protocol MUST reconcile the mounted routes with what the fetcher (and grok-cli) expect; do not design in a vacuum. GROUND TRUTH (verified 2026-10-04 against actual code): the two OKF clients were built against different imagined servers. Helix (src/okf/fetcher.rs) expects: GET {base}/okf/manifest.json, GET {base}/okf/bundles/{id}/manifest.json, GET {base}/okf/knowledge/{kid}, GET {base}/okf/health, optional Bearer auth_token, ETag/If-None-Match. grok-cli expects: POST {http(s)}://{server}:{port}/api/traces (default port 8080, 10s timeout, buffer-on-failure; src/workflow/okf.rs), POST {remote_url}/bundles/{bundle}/concepts (15s timeout; src/tools/okf_tools.rs push_concept_to_remote). grok-cli has NO remote fetch; Helix has NO push/trace. No single server satisfies both. CANONICAL v1 PROPOSAL (minimizes churn — Helix reads stay as-is): GET /okf/health -> 200 {"status":"ok"}; GET /okf/manifest.json and GET /okf/bundles/{id}/manifest.json -> manifest matching okf_bundle_schema.json (required: id, version); GET /okf/knowledge/{kid} -> document; POST /okf/traces (JSON WorkflowTrace, was grok-cli /api/traces); POST /okf/bundles/{bundle}/concepts (JSON OkfConcept, was grok-cli /bundles/{b}/concepts). Optional Bearer auth on all; ETag/If-None-Match on GETs; JSON error bodies {"error": ...}. WORK: write PROTOCOL.md (repo root or src/okf/) documenting every endpoint with request/response examples; update any Helix paths that deviate; grok-cli retarget is task grok-cli#480 (cross-repo — coordinate, do not duplicate). Contract tests: mock HTTP server asserting exact paths, methods, auth headers, ETag round-trip, and shape conformance to okf_bundle_schema.json.
tasks.results: PROTOCOL.md written at repo root (unified OKF v1: canonical /okf/* paths, auth/ETag/error conventions, client mapping table, migration notes). 6 Helix fetcher contract tests green against mockito mock server (canonical paths, Bearer, ETag 304 round-trip, schema conformance). No deviating paths remained in bot-repo; legacy grok-cli paths documented in PROTOCOL.md migration notes only.

tasks.description: New LLM tool so any backend (the 'commander' John chats with) can spin up a sub-agent on a chosen backend. This is the missing piece John hit on 2026-10-08: 'run a sub agent to plan out a bot app in rust' got clarifying questions because no such tool exists in src/tools/mod.rs.
tasks.details:
New file src/tools/subagent_tool.rs (or add to system_tools.rs — Ranger's call, keep it consistent with the module layout). Tool name: spawn_subagent. Params: task (string, required) — the marching orders; backend (string, optional) — one of local_ollama | lan_ollama | gemini | grok | auto (default auto); role_hint (string, optional) — planner | builder | reviewer | ui | free text. Dispatch design: reuse the A2A task-creation pattern (a2a/tasks.rs TaskStore::create) and run the prompt on the shared agent runtime loop (acp/agent.rs run_prompt) bound to the selected backend, exactly like a2a_handler.rs handle_message_send does with tokio::spawn. When backend=auto (or omitted), build a RoutingContext from the task text and call router::route() for the pick. Return to the commander: task id, chosen backend, and the sub-agent's final message (block with a configurable timeout; on timeout return partial status + task id so the commander can poll). Guardrails (non-negotiable): max spawn depth (a sub-agent may NOT spawn sub-agents beyond depth 1 — pass depth in and enforce, prevents infinite delegation loops); API-backend calls increment the spend counter used by task 217. Wire into execute() match in src/tools/mod.rs AND add the JSON schema to static_tool_definitions() (the file's own docs demand they stay in sync; there is a test asserting definitions are stable). Branch: PreRelese. Update CHANGELOG.md.

[Ranger 1 2026-10-08] Built. Deviations from plan: (1) did NOT reuse A2A TaskStore/run_prompt — no global TaskStore exists and run_prompt's AcpPlanner can only call system_status, useless for real sub-agent work. The runner drives the backend's native chat-with-tools loop (Ollama) or single-shot prompt (Gemini) instead. (2) On timeout the worker is cancelled; no poll-after-timeout registry (follow-up candidate). (3) Grok returns 'not implemented' — no client exists in the codebase. All 8 subagent + 4 spend unit tests pass; 6 pre-existing suite failures (a2a/acp/mcp_client) confirmed unrelated via clean-tree run. Zero new warnings.

Rules: (1) explicit backend param on spawn_subagent always wins (this is also John's manual UI override path via user_override); (2) backend=auto builds a RoutingContext and calls router::route() — note route() currently never selects LanOllama, decide its role (overflow/embeddings box at 192.168.1.149 vs general) and wire it in or document why not; (3) health-aware fallback: RoutingContext already carries health — if the chosen backend is unhealthy, walk down the ladder; (4) cost caps: [router] daily_api_cap_usd (default 5.00); every Gemini/Grok call decrements; at cap, paid backends are refused with a message routed to John (web UI notice + log) and the job falls back to local or waits.
